result:
I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Run with the same method on Q2, my calculation reproduces all 10 of your reference values exactly.

**Two things I had to fix to match your Q2 numbers**
1. **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (it ends in `Z`). Counting it as UTC put orders in the wrong month, so a, c, d, g and h didn't match. Shifting to Korean time (+9 hours) before deciding the quarter and month fixed them.
2. **Duplicate customers:** there are 300 customer rows but only 250 distinct emails once case and spaces are ignored. For the customer counts (b, f) and the refund leader (e), I treated rows with the same email as one customer. For a, each order uses the segment on its own customer row, after trimming and lowercasing (`SMB`, `smb` → `smb`). That is what reproduces your Q2 value; duplicate rows of the same email sometimes have different segments.

There is no April data, so Q2 really only covers May and June.

**Q3 results**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment / net sales | `smb` / 307,141,008 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 248 |
| c. Top category / net sales | `sw` / 278,886,059 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with largest total refunds | u95@ex.com (2,065,000; no tie) |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 236 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 712,511 |
| h. Growth, Sep vs Aug | -1.4% |

Monthly net sales: July 276,419,108, August 306,752,176, September 302,481,111. For h, (302,481,111 − 306,752,176) / 306,752,176 = −1.392%, which rounds to −1.4%. I checked the e ranking and the monthly totals with separate SQL queries, and they agree.

STATUS: DONE
